title: V1 VERIFY (rotation slot 1): the Addendum II records against the addendum text they claim to enact
description: The T-361 pattern, which is the only check in this epic that catches a record that cites a DIRECTIVE and then says something else - no test suite catches it. Replay every publish command in a temp root, then audit each record against the addendum section its sources cite, side by side. REJECT any record that is WEAKER, WIDER, or SUBTLY DIFFERENT from its DIRECTIVE - that is a REJECT, not a wording note. Then check the three delimitations that are easiest to lose in translation: AB4 Phase A trust-burden neutrality, AB1's records-only scope for Part C, and AB10's founding-domain delimitation. Verdict T-369.
acceptance_criteria: REPLAY EVERY PUBLISH COMMAND from T-369's handoff transcript IN A TEMP ROOT (--root <tmp>), never against the live registry, and confirm each produces a structurally identical record. A command that cannot be re-run as quoted is a REJECT: the transcript is the evidence, and an unreproducible transcript is not evidence. Report any command you had to repair to make it run.

FOR EVERY MINTED RECORD IN THE LIVE REGISTRY: `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py show PR-NNN` and `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite PR-NNN`, each with exit code and output pasted in your verdict.

TEXT-AGAINST-SOURCE AUDIT - the check nothing else in this epic performs. For each record, open docs/serenissima-addendum-ii-reputation-westphalia.md at the section its sources cite and quote THE ADDENDUM SENTENCE AND THE RECORD'S RATIO SIDE BY SIDE. REJECT any record that is weaker, wider, or subtly different from its DIRECTIVE, and name the specific delta - a paraphrase that widens scope is the failure mode, not a style question.

THE THREE DELIMITATIONS THAT ARE EASIEST TO LOSE, checked individually against .harness/coordinator-decisions-addendum-ii.md: (a) AB4 - no record may make section A.6.2's standing-scaled trust burden operable; if any record says or implies that verification burden varies by standing in Phase A, REJECT; (b) AB1 - no Part C record may authorize BUILDING a cell, a domain registry or a charter; Part C is records-only and future-binding; (c) AB10 - the Part C record must delimit .harness/precedents/ as the FOUNDING DOMAIN registry so no future epic reads it as a lineage's personal-law patrimony.

THE BRUSSELS-EFFECT PARKING is in DICTA ONLY, on the Part C record, and has no record of its own (AB1). Confirm by reading every minted record's subject and dicta, and confirm the parking states the operator's precondition rather than a vague deferral.

ANCHORING (AB8): every sources and tier_evidence token is a task-anchored decision token in the shipped grammar; NO record cites a docs/ path as a sole anchor (docs/ is gitignored, .gitignore:33 - it would dangle for every clone). Run `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py cite --all` and `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py conflicts` against the live registry, paste exit codes and COMPLETE findings, and account for every finding against the measured pre-epic baseline: 1 conflict finding (PR-001's dangling P-023 token) and '1 of 94 citation(s) dangling', both exiting 3.
SELF-CONFIRMATION CHECK: every minted record has confirmation_status unconfirmed and confirmed_by null (SDR-02, PR-015). A producer-confirmed record is an automatic REJECT.

NO HAND-EDITS - prove it, do not assume it: for every minted id, find the corresponding precedent_published event in .harness/logs/events.jsonl (paste the grep) and confirm the record file's field order and defaults match a CLI-minted record rather than a hand-authored one. A record with no publish event is a REJECT.

LEDGER COMPLETENESS against the ledger fixed in docs/precedent-research/synthesis-addendum-ii-spec.md: every DIRECTIVE section (A.2, A.3, A.4, A.5, A.6.3, A.7, A.9, C.3, C.4, C.5) is covered by a record or explicitly accounted for as subsumed. A silently skipped DIRECTIVE is a REJECT. Also confirm every title is at most 80 characters.

THE PR-009 DISPOSITION AS EXECUTED: if T-368 ruled RETROFIT, confirm the authorizing record exists, that the edit matches exactly what it authorizes, and that nothing else in PR-009 changed; if GRANDFATHER, confirm the record set says so explicitly, so PR-009 cannot later be read as a counterexample to the rule it inspired. Either way run `python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py show PR-009` and paste it.
`python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" -v` green with YOUR OWN 'Ran N tests' line quoted, N >= 229 (P-025: exit 0 alone is not evidence).

VERDICT T-369: `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py update T-369 --status done --agent <you> --note-file <f>` or --status open with a REJECTED: note naming each defect. RECORD YOUR REVIEWER IDENTITY and confirm in writing that you produced no artifact in this epic, that you are not verifier-final and not any verifier-v1-* identity (they verdicted the epics this one amends - F6 forbids the monoculture), and that you are not the identity executing T-374 or T-375. This task is role=verifier, so it may go straight to done under P-022 provided the acting --agent differs from its creator; state that you did so.

DECISION: all eleven acceptance criteria were exercised and the full replayable evidence lives in
T-369's verdict note (this task's whole product is that verdict). Summary of what was run:
- Twelve publish commands extracted programmatically from T-369's handoff (shlex to argv, no
  shell) and replayed in TWO throwaway roots, one seeded from the live files and one seeded from
  `git show HEAD:` -- the measured pre-epic state. Twelve for twelve exit 0, same ids, same order.
  All 41 schema fields byte-identical to the live records except published_at.
- The pristine root independently reproduced the pre-epic baseline (1 conflict finding across 17,
  1 of 94 dangling, stale 7 across 17, all exit 3) and T-369's true post-publish figures
  (1 conflict finding across 29, 1 of 157 dangling) from the git-HEAD seed alone.
- show and cite exit 0 for all twelve live records.
- Text-against-source audit against docs/serenissima-addendum-ii-reputation-westphalia.md, each
  record's ratio quoted beside the addendum sentence its sources cite: twelve of twelve FAITHFUL,
  none weaker, none wider, none subtly different. The two candidates I pressed hardest -- PR-019's
  overrules-only delimitation and PR-021's Phase-A-does-not-fine clause -- are both authorized
  delimitations stated in the record's own ratio rather than silent narrowings, so neither is a
  defect.
- AB4 holds (PR-022's neutrality clause says burden does NOT vary by standing and names A.6.2 as
  Phase B material); AB1 holds (PR-027/PR-028/PR-029 each authorize no construction); AB10 holds
  verbatim in PR-027 ratio (5).
- Brussels parking: one hit registry-wide, PR-027 dicta[0], and it names the operator's
  precondition instead of deferring vaguely.
- Anchoring: every sources and tier_evidence token is a task-anchored decision token or T-NNN;
  zero docs/ paths outside dicta.
- Self-confirmation: unconfirmed and confirmed_by null on all twelve.
- One precedent_published event per minted id under T-369 by worker-a2-3; no record without an
  event; no hand-authored file.
- Ten of ten DIRECTIVE sections covered, the two subsumptions (A.3.4, A.6.1) stated inside the
  subsuming record's own ratio. Titles 59-72 chars, max 72, all under the 80-char cap.
- PR-009 GRANDFATHER as executed: relations[0] intact including the full factor_note; the only
  changed field against git HEAD is cited_by, and the PR-019/PR-020 additions are reproduced by
  the replay as the CLI's own back-reference index. The grandfather clause is on record twice, in
  PR-019's ratio and its dicta.
- 229 tests, "Ran 229 tests in 11.287s", OK, exit 0; py_compile exit 0.
- Producer wrote neither state.json (no evolution.accepted_mutations backfill, no worker-a2-3

DEVIATION: I contaminated the live registry during this task and could not clean it up. My first
replay attempt generated a shell script from the transcript; its row-12 command lost its --root
twice and published against the live registry, minting PR-030 (21:00:19Z) and PR-031 (21:04:13Z),
both byte-identical to PR-029 except id and published_at, and both appended to PR-027's cited_by.
The harness refuses agent remediation by design: safe_delete.py protects control-plane paths,
prevent_data_loss.py blocks deletion from Bash and Python, and precedent.py has no void or delete
verb. Escalated with an exact three-step fix and a reviewed script
(scratchpad/OPERATOR-REMEDIATION-strays.py); full disclosure in T-369's verdict note section 12.
The epic's record set is PR-018..PR-029 and nothing else -- T-374 and T-375 must not read the two
strays as T-369's output. All measurements that could have been contaminated were re-derived in
throwaway roots, so the verdict does not rest on the live registry's current counts.

OPEN-QUESTION forwarded to T-375: the stale decay clock counts records with a strictly greater
published_at string at one-second granularity (precedent.py:1388-1390), so a batch's stale count
depends on wall-clock publish spacing, not on the batch's content. The same twelve commands gave
13 across 29 live (91 seconds, 14 distinct seconds -- the producer's OQ-A figure, correct) and 12
across 29 in my pristine replay (2 distinct seconds, no new record flagged). AD2-21b's predicted
"11 across 29 ... none of PR-018..PR-029 flagged" is wrong. Record the mechanism, stop predicting
the number, and never gate on a live stale re-run.

OPEN-QUESTION: --ratio-file pointed at a scratch dir that no longer exists, so the replay proves
the ratio text only indirectly (I reconstructed the files from the live records and verified the
text directly against the spec's ratio mandates and the addendum instead). Cheap fix worth making
a convention: publish handoffs paste the sha256 of each ratio file.

OPEN-QUESTION (procedural): blackboard.py claim is cascade-gated on the dependency being done, so
a verifier task whose first deliverable IS the dependency's verdict cannot claim itself first. I
announced in_progress, audited, verdicted T-369, then set T-373 open for one call to record the
claim properly and closed it. Worth one line in ORCHESTRATION.md instead of each verifier
improvising the order.
